hints.title: Bypass Elimination Property
hints.text: Because query edges never cross each other, adding directed road (u, v) effectively bypasses and permanently removes all intermediate vertices between u and v from the shortest path.

hints.title: Jump-Pointer Tracking
hints.text: Maintain next pointers initialized to i + 1. When jumping from u to v, contract all bypassed links and update intermediate pointers to v directly.

hints.title: Amortized Link Deletion
hints.text: Each bypassed edge is compressed at most once across all queries, decrementing the total path distance by the number of compressed edges.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def shortestDistanceAfterQueries(self, n: int, queries: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        nxt = list(range(1, n)) + [0]
        dist = n - 1
        ans = []
        for u, v in queries:
            curr = nxt[u]
            while curr < v:
                dist -= 1
                temp = nxt[curr]
                nxt[curr] = v
                curr = temp
            nxt[u] = max(nxt[u], v)
            ans.append(dist)
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Each node pointer is bypassed at most once amortized.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Running breadth-first search per query gives O(q * n) which times out on large inputs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) next pointer array provides O(1) amortized updates.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizes non-crossing shortcut invariant and implements amortized jump pointer compression.
